name: Dill
grown_as: An annual herb sown in spring for its leaves and later its seed. Varieties (such as 'Bouquet' or 'Fernleaf') differ mainly in height.
habit: A single slender upright stem 60 to 120 cm tall, branching only near the top, the whole plant airy and see-through. Stem hollow, smooth, blue-green with fine pale stripes and a dusty bloom. Smells strongly of dill when touched.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate up the stem; the first leaves in a loose tuft from the base
leaf.type: Compound, three or four times pinnate: divided again and again into very fine thread-like segments
leaf.outline: Triangular overall, 10 to 30 cm long, the threads spreading mostly in one flat plane like a feather
leaf.base: The leaf stalk widens into a broad sheath that wraps the stem, with pale papery edges
leaf.tip: Each thread ends in a fine soft point
leaf.margin: No teeth: the segments are threads 1 to 2 cm long and well under 1 mm wide
leaf.veins: Not seen: each thread is a single vein
leaf.stalk: Short above the sheath; upper leaves sit almost straight on their sheaths
leaf.colour: Blue-green to grey-green, paler than fennel

flower.form: Flat-topped compound umbels like an open umbrella, made of many tiny flowers
flower.petals: Five tiny yellow petals per flower, their tips rolled inwards so each flower looks like a dot
flower.centre: Each tiny flower has a yellow swollen base (stylopodium) and five yellow stamens
flower.behind: No bracts under the umbel and no bracteoles under the small umbels: the rays are bare
flower.carried: At the top of the stem and its branches, facing up. The main umbel 10 to 15 cm across with 15 to 40 rays of unequal length, each ending in a small round umbel
flower.size: Each flower about 1 to 2 mm; the whole umbel up to 15 cm

fruit: Flat oval seeds 3 to 5 mm long in pairs, brown with three fine ribs on the face and a pale flat wing round the edge. They ripen from green to brown on the open umbrella of rays and fall easily.
seedling: Two long, very narrow seed leaves (2 to 3 cm, like green needles), then first true leaves already cut into threads
winter: Nothing: an annual that dies after seeding

leaf: divided three or four times into fine threads
a broad sheath with pale edges where the stalk meets the stem
bloom: a flat umbrella of many rays with no bracts at their base
tiny yellow flowers in small round umbels at the ray tips
flowers read as dots, not as petalled flowers
seed: flat oval seed, brown, with a pale wing round the edge
young: one upright stem with feathery thread-like leaves
sheathing leaf bases on the stem
crop: a single tall stem with airy blue-green feathery leaves
flower: flat yellow umbrellas at the top of a single slender stem
seedhead: brown umbrella of stiff rays with flat winged seeds in pairs
stem and leaves yellowing or dead

look_alikes: Fennel is a perennial with several stems, more three-dimensional leaves with longer threads and seeds without a wing. Chamomiles and mayweeds have thread-like leaves but daisy flowers.
